key_insight: BRACE jointly learns a Bayesian belief over user intent and a policy for assistance in an end-to-end way, so inference and assistance are optimized together rather than treated separately. This yields more adaptive, context-aware assistance that preserves user agency in unstructured environments.
problem_solved: Current shared-autonomy systems use fixed blending or decoupled goal inference and arbitration, producing suboptimal assistance when user intent and environment context are uncertain; BRACE addresses this by integrating belief estimation and policy optimization.
method: End-to-end training that backpropagates through a Bayesian belief module and a reinforcement-learning policy so belief updates and assistance actions are jointly optimized.
Context encoding to represent environment and user signals, producing a posterior over goals that conditions the assistance policy.
Reinforcement learning objective balances task performance and user agency, enabling adaptive assistance levels rather than static blending.
impact: Practitioners get a recipe for principled, adaptive shared-autonomy systems that improve task success under uncertainty while respecting user control; applicable to assistive robotics, teleoperation, and human-in-the-loop systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensor/user input → context encoder → Bayesian belief (posterior) → RL policy → robot action, with end-to-end gradient arrows.
Comparison bar chart: BRACE vs static blending and decoupled methods on success rate and user-override frequency.
Belief evolution heatmap: probability over candidate goals over time as user inputs arrive and assistance adapts.
Icon set: human operator, robot actuator, Bayesian prior/posterior, reward/gauge indicating assistance level.
paper_title: End-to-end Optimization of Belief and Policy Learning in Shared Autonomy Paradigms
paper_authors: MH Farhadi, Ali Rabiee, Sima Ghafoori, Anna Cetera, Andrew Fisher
